title: Machine learning phenotyping improves stroke GWAS power and flags an ABCG8 variant
summary: QTPhenProxy assigns each person in a cohort a machine-learned probability of having stroke from electronic health records, which was used as a quantitative trait in a GWAS. With an order of magnitude fewer cases than the largest stroke GWAS it recovered known variants better than previous methods and found a novel ABCG8 variant for intracerebral hemorrhage in UK Biobank, replicated in the MEGASTROKE meta-analysis. This is the first posted bioRxiv version; the published version may differ.
organization: Columbia University Irving Medical Center; Columbia University

evidence.tested: Variant recovery against previous methods and replication of an ABCG8 association in MEGASTROKE.
evidence.unknown: Preprint; published version may differ; replication used existing data; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning model converting EHR data into disease probabilities for association testing.
